narrative:
##SUMMARY##
Funding conditions show mixed signals this week. Overnight rates are largely steady with SOFR up to 3.95 percent and EFFR unchanged at 3.88 percent. Repo rates are nudging lower, DVP Repo fell to 3.96 percent while Tri-Party and GCF repos edged higher to 3.95 and 3.99 percent. Total bank credit expanded to $20.01 trillion and commercial loans rose to $2.96 trillion, indicating more lending capacity. At the same time large and small bank deposits slipped and total bank assets contracted, pointing to some pressure on liquidity. Overall the picture is neither clearly tighter nor looser but a balance of modest easing in rates and modest growth in credit.

##FRESH:sofr##
SOFR rose to 3.95 percent for 2026-11-02, up 0.02 percentage points from the prior period. The increase signals a slight tightening of short-term funding costs. Higher SOFR can make borrowing a bit more expensive.

##FRESH:effr##
EFFR held at 3.88 percent for 2026-11-02, unchanged from the prior reading. Stability suggests funding conditions are steady at the federal funds level. No immediate pressure from this rate.

##FRESH:iorb##
IORB held at 3.9 percent for 2026-11-02, unchanged from the prior reading. The unchanged rate indicates no shift in overnight bank funding costs. Conditions remain flat.

##FRESH:bank_credit_total##
Total Bank Credit rose to $20.01 trillion for 2026-10-21, up $28.9 billion from the prior period. The rise points to expanding credit supply. This eases funding conditions.

##FRESH:commercial_loans##
Commercial Loans rose to $2.96 trillion for 2026-09-01, up $24.5 billion from the prior period. The growth shows more corporate borrowing. It suggests looser credit conditions.

##FRESH:dvp_overnight_rate##
DVP Repo Rate fell to 3.96 percent for 2026-11-04, down 0.02 percentage points from the prior period. The drop indicates a modest easing of repo funding costs. This supports slightly looser liquidity.

##RECENT##
Tri-Party Repo Rate rose to 3.95 percent, up 0.02 points; GCF Repo Rate rose to 3.99 percent, up 0.02 points; M2 Money Supply rose to $23.41 trillion, up $113.0 billion. Treasury General Account fell to $957.2 billion, down $42.6 billion; Overnight Reverse Repo rose to $5.1 billion, up $4.9 billion; Large Bank Deposits fell to $19.77 trillion, down $31.7 billion. Small Bank Deposits fell to $5.69 trillion, down $1.9 billion; Total Bank Assets fell to $26.08 trillion, down $45.9 billion. Foreign Official Treasury Holdings fell to $3.76 trillion, down $17.6 billion; Japan Treasury Holdings fell to $1.07 trillion, down $35.7 billion; China Treasury Holdings fell to $590.7 billion, down $27.3 billion; UK Treasury Holdings rose to $1.01 trillion, up $11.1 billion.

##WATCH##
Watch for any moves in SOFR and EFFR that could shift short-term funding costs. Monitor bank credit growth against the backdrop of falling deposits and assets. Keep an eye on repo rate trends and Treasury cash balances for signs of liquidity pressure.
